sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Adair County, KY?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work in Adair County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the assessed value of every parcel, and the sheriff collects the tax bill. Neither one sets the tax rate: that comes from the county, school district and special districts that levy the tax.

The Adair County PVA is at 424 Public Square, Suite 2, in Columbia, KY 42728. The phone is (270) 384-3673 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The PVA's staff handles deed transfers (including partial sales), vehicle value adjustments and homestead applications. The county's contact list also gives the Adair County Sheriff at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky fixes the assessment date at January 1, and all real property is valued as of that day. Someone who buys a house after January 1 will normally see the first bill under the previous owner's name, so a buyer and seller in Adair County should settle at closing who covers the bill for that year.

sections.h2: When are Adair County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Kentucky's regular schedule runs on the calendar year after assessment, and the sheriff accepts payment at each stage. Under KRS 134.015, paying in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount. From November 2 through December 31 the face amount is due. A 5 percent penalty applies in January, and a 10 percent penalty applies after January 31.

Kentucky regular collection schedule for real property (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

If bills go out late, the state can use an alternative schedule that gives one month for the discount, one month at face, and one month at the 5 percent penalty. Unpaid bills move to the county clerk after April 15, where they become certificates of delinquency and a lien is recorded against the parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Adair County assessment?
sections.html:
You start with a conference at the PVA's office, and only then can you file an appeal. The tax roll is open for public inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May. If you disagree with the value, ask for the conference during that window, or earlier once assessment notices are mailed.

  • Meet with the PVA or a deputy. They must explain how the value was set and keep a written record of the conference.
  • File the appeal at the County Clerk's office by the end of the next workday after the inspection period closes.
  • Bring evidence: physical details of the land and improvements, insurance policies, construction costs and real estate listings or sales. The local board denies an appeal that lacks documentation.
  • Attend the hearing, which is held 25 to 35 days after inspection ends. Skipping it forfeits any further appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Anyone paid to represent you must be an attorney, CPA, certified real estate appraiser or a licensed Kentucky broker or appraiser, and must show written authorization from you. Most appeals finish before bills are printed. If the board sets a higher value than you claimed, a supplemental bill follows.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Adair County?
sections.html:
Yes. Kentucky homeowners who are 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled, can have part of the assessment removed. The state Department of Revenue sets the amount at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. On a house assessed at $150,800, the Census median value for Adair County, the taxable assessment would be $101,700.

Applications go to the Adair County PVA by mail, fax or email in the year the exemption is wanted. Proof of age can be a driver's license, Medicare card, birth certificate or a similar record, and a Kentucky license or state ID shows residence. Only one exemption is allowed per household, and when one spouse is 65 the age requirement is met.

An approved exemption carries forward as long as the applicant owns and lives in the home. A seller should tell the PVA once the house is sold so the exemption comes off that address and can be claimed again at the new one.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell an Adair County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax debt stays with the property. Kentucky law makes the taxes a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and the lien that attaches to a delinquent parcel lasts until the taxes are paid or the 11-year period under KRS 134.420 runs out, no matter who owns the house. A buyer's title search will find it, so call the sheriff for a payoff figure before listing.

After the sheriff transfers an unpaid bill to the county clerk, 1 percent interest is added for each month, plus clerk and county attorney commissions and a lien recording fee. The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and later a second notice. A tax sale can then be held 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and a third-party purchaser may buy the certificate and add its own charges.

Paying the sheriff before the April 15 transfer keeps the clerk's commissions, monthly interest and lien fee off the bill, which makes the weeks before that date the cheapest time to settle an overdue balance.

sections.h2: What is Adair County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Adair County was formed in 1801 from part of Green County, and Columbia is both the county seat and its only city. It covers about 405 square miles of land on the Pennyroyal Plateau, with more than 40 percent of the land in timber. The Green River runs through the county and was dammed to form Green River Lake, which anchors Green River Lake State Park.

The economy is largely agricultural, with livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco, and the Cumberland Parkway, finished in 1973, eased the county's long road isolation. Adair County Schools serves students from primary through high school. Census QuickFacts gives this snapshot:

  • Population: 19,423 in 2025, up 2.8 percent since 2020.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.2 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $150,800.
  • Median household income: $53,553, with 21.2 percent of people in poverty.
  • Median gross rent: $771.

Only six building permits were issued in 2025, so most sales are of existing houses. For a property with deferred repairs or back taxes, a cash sale to a buyer who closes as-is can remove the repair and tax questions in one transaction.

faqs.q: When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?
faqs.a: November 1. Kentucky law gives a 2 percent discount to anyone who pays the whole bill by that date. From November 2 to December 31 the bill is due at face value, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Adair County?
faqs.a: Payment goes to the Adair County Sheriff, who collects the bill. The PVA at (270) 384-3673 values the property but does not collect. The county contact list shows the sheriff's office at (270) 384-2776.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, set by the Kentucky Department of Revenue and subtracted from assessed value. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and you apply through the Adair County PVA.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?
faqs.a: No. You must first confer with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk by the end of the workday after the roll inspection period closes. That period starts the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days.

faqs.q: What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: After April 15 the bill passes to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien on the property and 1 percent monthly interest. A tax sale may follow 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
